tool_args.rationale: The pilot covers H = 0.16–0.48, far short of the target H = 21.1. Over the pilot window, the slow adaptation term can look nearly linear in H, so different amplitude–time constant pairs can fit the pilot yet yield materially different forecasts, including different signs. The slow-horizon probe directly tests that ambiguity.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the five-parameter sink-coupled model now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The five short-horizon rows do not reliably separate the slow adaptation amplitude from its time constant.
Finer sampling is less informative than observing the response near the forecast horizon, where slow adaptation can become distinguishable.
It omits the gradient dependence suggested by the lower response per unit input in the high-gradient pilot rows.
